items.description: Waymo 宣布进入加拿大，将在多伦多布局完全自动驾驶出行服务，目标2028年迎接首批乘客。近期将先以人工驾驶方式采集高精地图并由自动驾驶专家进行测试；Waymo 与 Element Fleet Management 合作提供车队管理服务，将逐步创造数百个岗位。官方称基于超4亿公里完全自动驾驶里程，其车辆在严重伤害及以上事故中比人类驾驶少95%。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/xwgy3mhme6nur9kndswxlu0es

items.title: 丹麦最高法院裁定持有传播 AI 生成儿童色情内容可判实刑
items.description: 据彭博社 15 日报道，丹麦最高法院维持对一名 31 岁男子 18 个月监禁的判决，该男子因持有并传播 3.6 万余张 AI 生成的儿童色情图像获刑，且不适用缓刑。法院裁定，即使图像无真实人物原型，也受丹麦《刑法》约束，量刑时不应考虑人物是否虚构；此案为丹麦首起此类定罪，并引发跨国调查，警方查明 273 名买家身份、逮捕 25 人。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/bvljy29i9xwh3wnkwign3npt4

items.title: 亚马逊云科技 CFO 称 AI 基建的繁荣可持续，AI 服务器投资回报周期不到三年
items.description: IT之家 10 月 18 日消息，据 Axios 于当地时间 10 月 16 日报道，亚马逊云科技（AWS）首席财务官约翰 · 费尔顿（John Felton）表示， 人工智能基础设施与服务支出的繁荣是可持续的 ，因为它正在推动有意义的创新。 随着债务规模膨胀、估值高企以及循环融资交易频现，部分投资者与分析师对“AI 泡沫”愈发焦虑，担忧企业的营收增速能否跟上数额庞大的基建投入。 约翰 · 费尔顿表示，公司的 AI 资本支出正在带来回报，其切身经验也证明，在 AI 领域大举投入能够获得收益。他认为， 看待 AI 的成熟方式是将其视为生产力提升工具 ，而不仅是“降本工具”。 费尔顿表示，截至第二季度，公司拥有近 5,000 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 3.35 万亿元人民币） 的在手订单储备，基于此他对当前的资本支出“感到踏实”。这笔储备由庞大客群共同支撑 ——“既涵盖行业巨头、顶级 AI 实验室，也包括中小企业”。 费尔顿透露，AWS 的 AI 服务器投资正在取得丰硕成果，“在这些服务器上， 我们看到的投资回报周期不到三年 。” 数据显示，AWS 第二季度实现营收 422 亿美元

items.title: Anthropic 联合创始人：到 2030 年 AI 有望推动美国 GDP 增长近 50%
items.description: IT之家 10 月 18 日消息，Anthropic 联合创始人杰克 · 克拉克（Jack Clark）于当地时间周六表示，人工智能能力的快速进步，将推动各行各业发生更迅猛的变革。该公司内部模型预测，在特定条件下，到 2030 年 AI 能让美国经济产出提升近 50%。 克拉克在曼谷举办的国际货币基金组织与世界银行年会上发言称，需要开展国际合作，为这项具备变革性的技术制定“非同寻常且严格的规则”，政策制定者的行动窗口期正在不断收窄。 克拉克表示，预估美国 GDP 将达到 44 万亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 294.93 万亿元人民币），而当前 GDP 略高于 30 万亿美元（现汇率约合 201.09 万亿元人民币）。“我知道这个数字听起来非常离谱。”但他补充，AI 正在极大加速科学发现。 他提到，该预测的前提是“技术持续迭代进步。倘若 GDP 实现如此大幅度增长，经济学理论认为，必须诞生新产业与新发明，才能支撑这样规模的经济扩张。” 克拉克发表此番言论之际，Anthropic 正筹备预计 11 月进行的首次公开募股，估值最高可达 2 万亿美元（现汇率约合 13.41 万亿元人民币）

items.title: Anthropic 报告：AI 重塑公司用工结构，初级技术岗招聘明显收缩
items.description: IT之家 10 月 18 日消息，Anthropic 于当地时间周五发布的一份报告显示，过去一年里，公司员工构成与业务工作形态都发生了显著变化。 Anthropic 认为，该公司内部的职场变化趋势，能够预示“人工智能将如何改变整个经济体的工作组织方式、招聘模式与劳动力需求”，尤其是因为这家企业已经“围绕人工智能深度重塑了自身工作流程”。即便其他机构不会像 Anthropic 这样全面、或是采用完全相同的方式落地 AI，这份报告也为外界提供了一个有趣的窗口，一窥该公司当下的运营模式。 值得关注的是， Anthropic 正在减少初级岗位招聘 。自 2025 年初以来，技术部门初级员工占比从 21% 下降至 14%，初级技术岗新员工占比降幅更大，由 27% 跌至 9%。 Anthropic 还提到，技术团队在全体员工中的占比有所下降，从 61% 降至 56%。公司将该趋势归因于“企业规模扩张过程中业务职能板块的自然扩充”，同时还有“代码工具让非技术员工能够自行开发软件”这一因素。 据转述，有员工表示在 Anthropic 长期承受着压力，需要尽可能加快进度，凡事都用 Claude 来完成。

items.title: OpenAI 将研发人形机器人，奥尔特曼称核心是打造“大脑”
items.description: IT之家 10 月 18 日消息，尽管 OpenAI 已经忙于开发人工智能模型和全新消费级硬件，但首席执行官萨姆 · 奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）及其团队显然还有精力推进另一个项目：人形机器人。 奥尔特曼在《Sources》播客节目中解释，选择人形具备合理性，原因是“这个世界本身就是为人类设计的”。门、键盘和各类工具，都是按照特定人体形态打造。一台要在同类空间内活动的机器人，采用相近外形会是合适的选择。正如奥尔特曼所说：“匹配这种外形是个不错的思路。” 被问到 OpenAI 是否会亲自制造人形机器人时，他的回答十分简洁：“我们会。”不过奥尔特曼并不十分在意机器人外观这类细碎细节。他称，这些问题“远不如真正研发出驱动机器人运转的‘大脑’重要”。简单来讲，如果一台机器不知道如何运用四肢，就算给它装上双臂双腿，也难以发挥作用。 IT之家注意到，该项目距离成为正式产品还有很长一段路。奥尔特曼在接受《财富》杂志采访时表示：“我预计我们会在 2027 年拿出亮眼的演示样机…… 但机器人走上街头还需要再等好几年。”OpenAI 没有透露这场演示会展示哪些内容、人形机器人长什么样，以及外部人员何时

items.content: 由于 Claude 写代码的速度实在太快，在 Anthropic 内部真正的瓶颈反而是人类过去几十年发明的软件工具，它们已经开始处理不了 AI 7×24 生产力的代码。 没办法，Anthropic 用一个 7 人团队，还是用 Claude，用 5 个月的时间，从零打造了一套全新的代码版本控制系统，把整个大仓库迁过去。 今年 5 月，Anthropic 整个公司平均每天合并（Merge，即代码通过审核正式入库）的代码变更大约是 2500 次，这完全是一家大型科技公司相当活跃的水平。 如果换算成时间，意味着 24 小时不间断，平均每 2.8 秒，就有一段经过测试和审查的新代码被放进 Anthropic 的核心代码库里。 更可怕的是 「我们预计这种增长速度短期内根本不会放缓。内部对合并代码的潜在需求几乎是无限的，我们每扫除一个基础设施瓶颈，代码产量就会立刻迎来下一波暴涨。」 很多非技术背景但关注 AI 的朋友，可能经常听说 GitHub 上多少多少个 Star 的项目，GitHub 就是全球最大的开源社区，也是无数 AI 项目的发源地，Meta 的 Llama、DeepSeek 的开源模型，代码都托管在上面。

items.title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
items.description: A Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web.
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: Last day to save up to $200 to TechCrunch Founder Summit on Oct. 16. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Meta recently updated its commercial terms of use, declaring that the company can “use any content from [a business account’s] domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta products and services. According to legal experts interviewed by Nieman Lab , this looked like a “remarkable provision” that could give Meta permission to scrape the website of any publisher with a Meta business account and use the content to train the company’s AI models. (While Meta defeated a high-profile lawsuit over alleged copyright infringement last year, other cases against AI companies, including Meta, continue.) However, a Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web. And now, The Verge reports that the provision has been removed. “We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves,” the company said in a statement. “It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers.”

items.description: The composition of Anthropic’s workforce and the type of work getting done have changed significantly in the past year.
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: Last day to save up to $200 to TechCrunch Founder Summit on Oct. 16. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. The composition of Anthropic’s workforce and the type of work getting done have changed significantly in the past year, according to a report that the AI company published on Friday. Anthropic argues that its own workplace trends could be indicators of “how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy,” especially since the company “has thoroughly molded its workflows around AI.” But even if other organizations never embrace AI as thoroughly or in the exact same way as Anthropic, the report offers an intriguing glimpse at how the company currently operates. Notably, Anthropic is making fewer junior hires, with the proportion of junior-level employees in technical departments falling from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and the proportion of junior technical hires falling even more sharply, from 27% to 9%. Anthropic also says that technical teams now represent a smaller share of the overall workforce, falling from 61% to 56% — a trend that it attributes to  “natural expansion of business functions as the company scales,” as well as “coding tools increasingly allowing non-technical employees to make software themselves.”

Replit, the AI coding platform that has become a favorite of startup founders and developers, is no longer working with Anthropic, the company’s CEO and co-founder Amjad Masad said Thursday while onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt . Masad said the decision was made for a number of different reasons, including cost. Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer partnering with Anthropic. “I think ChatGPT is better now,” Masad said, adding that the company uses an internal benchmark to help assess metrics like performance. “We publish a public benchmark as well, and consistently, Sol and Astra perform better on building vibe-coded applications from scratch. It was a decision based on both cost, partnership, and performance. And for all these reasons, we just felt like they were a better partner for now.” It seems, however, that Anthropic hasn’t been completely cut out of Replit, which sells a cloud-based software development platform where users can develop and deploy apps directly from inside their browser.

items.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
items.description: The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles.
items.author: Aditya Mehta
items.content: Last day to save up to $200 to TechCrunch Founder Summit on Oct. 16. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. AI agents from multiple providers accessed personal data and confidential material at Indian organizations during research and testing, India’s cybersecurity agency said Thursday. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it had received “multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers” whose models, during research and evaluation runs on the open internet, “had reached the live systems of Indian organizations.” The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles, and their actions “exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks.” This makes India the latest stop on what has become a world tour for rogue AI agents. In July, OpenAI’s agents escaped a test environment and hacked French company Hugging Face — kicking off a summer of rogue AI agent activity. Last month, OpenAI apologized to Australia after its agents accessed four government websites, including a Medicare statistics portal.

items.title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
items.description: According to Elorian's evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.
items.author: Aditya Mehta
items.content: Last day to save up to $200 to TechCrunch Founder Summit on Oct. 16. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Elorian , the Palo Alto AI startup that raised a $55 million seed round at a $300 million valuation before it launched a product, released its first model on Friday, TechCrunch has exclusively learned. The model, Glimpse , is launching as a research preview with API access and a chat interface. The thesis? Today’s AI models, for all their skill with language and code, still can’t really see. Most multimodal models look at an image once, convert it to tokens, and then reason about it in text — like describing a photo from memory. Glimpse keeps going back to the source. Mid-reasoning, it can crop into a region, pull specific frames from a video, or run code to measure or compare what it’s looking at, a mechanism Elorian calls a “visual scratch space.” Think of someone pinching to zoom on a phone photo to double-check what they thought they saw. For former Google DeepMind researcher and Elorian CEO Andrew Dai, one of the clearest signs that AI still couldn’t really see came on game night.
